primitives.name: Ball Freak Formation
primitives.verbatim_quote: They then jump to the new distribution and ball goes into play without signal.
primitives.assumptions: Players act as coordinated units, simultaneous position shifts eliminate pre-snap hesitation, and the absence of a formal snap signal creates timing uncertainty for defenders.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs when defensive coordination fails to track rapid, synchronized offensive repositioning, leading to exploitable gaps.

layer2.mapping: GSI - Joint probability distributions over player states; GSE - Simultaneous state transitions without explicit trigger signals.
layer2.telemetry: Average time differential between offensive shift completion and ball movement, defensive misalignment rate

primitives.name: Elbow Charge Technique
primitives.verbatim_quote: Heffelfinger is said to have charged his opponent with his elbow, holding his hands locked while doing so.
primitives.assumptions: Locked hands create a rigid mechanical advantage, focusing impact force through the olecranon process of the ulna to maximize collision momentum.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs when the defender adjusts stance to absorb lateral force, converting linear momentum into rotational energy.

layer2.mapping: GSI - Rigid-body collision mechanics with fixed contact points; GSE - High-impact frontal blocking strategies.
layer2.telemetry: Impact velocity at point of contact, defender's angular displacement during collision

primitives.name: Uppercut Jolt Technique
primitives.verbatim_quote: Brown had a tremendous uppercutting jolt which he used to turn his opponent aside.
primitives.assumptions: The upward force vector generates vertical lift, disrupting the opponent's center of mass and redirecting their horizontal momentum.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity arises when the defender's base of support is too wide or they brace downward, negating the vertical impulse.

layer2.mapping: GSI - Vertical impulse transfer creating temporary instability; GSE - Redirective force application to alter trajectory.
layer2.telemetry: Angle of applied force relative to ground, change in opponent's vertical velocity

primitives.name: Spring Frame Principle
primitives.verbatim_quote: His tremendous frame was drawn down like a powerful spring.
primitives.assumptions: Muscular tension stores elastic potential energy that converts to kinetic energy upon release, amplifying initial acceleration.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs when the stored energy dissipates through inefficient force vectors or premature deceleration.

layer2.mapping: GSI - Elastic energy storage and release in player movement; GSE - Explosive state transitions from preparatory positions.
layer2.telemetry: Pre-contact compression distance, post-release velocity magnitude
